correctness.rationale: For F=f6/(f1 f2 f3), Kassel--Reutenauer Theorem 1.1 gives the reciprocal coefficients as signed rational multiples of the sum-of-two-squares count, hence [q^(4n+3)]F^{-1}=0 identically. The integral Frobenius relation H(q)^(2^t) congruent H(q^2)^(2^(t-1)) modulo 2^t, applied twice, yields F^(k+1) congruent to a q^4-series modulo 2^(s-1) where s=nu2(k+1)>=2. Multiplication by F^{-1} proves the lower bound for all n; s=1 is trivial. The explicit first index A_k(3)=k(k+1)(k+14)/6 has exactly valuation s-1 because k and k+14 are odd. This also certifies all quantifiers and boundaries. The attached checker passed 40 inverse-gap tests, 2600 divisibility tests, 65 first-index sharpness tests and 81 independent reciprocal comparisons; these finite checks do not establish infinite validity.

value.rationale: Conjecture 6.1 in the November 2026 primary manuscript asks for the highest uniform dyadic divisibility of designated multipartition counts on 4n+3, a mathematically natural and explicitly posed problem. The result proves the complete odd-k half, including unbounded exponents as k+1 gains powers of two, rather than isolated finite cases. The use of the exact reciprocal theta support and a sharp index-three obstruction explains the structure and optimality. It does not assert the unsolved even-k classification.
